citation.authors: Hoshi D, Fukuie M, Hashitomi T, Tarumi T, Sugawara J, Watanabe K
citation.title: Respiratory function and breathing response to water- and land-based cycling at the matched oxygen uptake

population.description: Twelve healthy men (Methods 2.2: mean age 24 +/- 1 years, BMI 22.3 +/- 1.6 kg/m2; Data are presented as mean +/- SD). Screened by medical history questionnaire: no overt cardiovascular, respiratory or neuromuscular disease, no medication, no smoking. Age and BMI as printed; no minimum or maximum printed.

protocols.name: land_cycling
protocols.description: Land-based cycling day (LC, day 3) from the start of the seated rest. Arm minutes 0 to 4: 5 min seated on land (Methods: 'rested in the seated position on land for 5 min'). Minutes 5 to 8: 4 min on the semi-recumbent bicycle (hip angle about 130 deg; 'rested for another 4 min on a semi-recumbent bicycle'), read as seated rest; no load is stated. Minutes 9 to 23: 15 min of cycling at 60 rpm, three 5-min stages ('wattage was adjusted ... at the beginning and every 5 min'): stage 1 minutes 9 to 13, stage 2 minutes 14 to 18, stage 3 minutes 19 to 23. Duration 5 + 4 + 15 = 24 min. Intensity from the measured VO2 of each stage (Table 1, LC, ml/kg/min; mean of the last 30 s of the stage), level = (VO2 - 3.7) / 31.7: stage 1 (5.8 - 3.7) / 31.7 = 0.0662, stage 2 (9.4 - 3.7) / 31.7 = 0.1798, stage 3 (17.1 - 3.7) / 31.7 = 0.4227. The rest VO2 (3.1 ml/kg/min) is below 3.7, so rest is level 0. The printed watts (12.9, 44.6 and 105.0 W; Results 3.1) are not used, since the measured VO2 is. Food before the visit is 'fast for a minimum of 3 h' (Methods 2.3), a lower bound with no last meal and no contents, so the fed state is unknown: norm_center start, no meal. Clock hour not printed: 8.0 assumed.

findings.description: Heart rate at seated rest before land cycling: mean of the readings at 2 and 4 min of the 4-min bicycle rest (Methods 2.4.1: HR 'intermittently measured at 2- and 4-min during rest ... and averaged'), arm minutes 7 and 9, entered as the window [7, 9) just before cycling starts at minute 9. SD, n = 12.

location.where: Table 1, 'HR, bpm' block, row 'Rest', column LC

findings.description: Oxygen uptake at seated rest before land cycling: mean of the last 30 s of the 4-min bicycle rest (Methods 2.4.1: 'average of the last 30 s during each stage'), read as the window [8, 9). SD, n = 12. ml/min as printed.

location.where: Table 1, 'VO2, ml/min' block, row 'Rest', column LC

findings.description: Respiratory rate at stage 3 of land cycling (the last of three 5-min stages, arm minutes 19 to 23, VO2 17.1 ml/kg/min): mean of the last 30 s of the stage, which the paper names as the steady-state window (Methods 2.4.1: 'these variables were averaged over the last 30 s of the resting and cycling conditions'; 'all metabolic and breathing parameters reached a steady state'), read as the window [23, 24). Printed 'bpm'; it is breaths per minute. SD, n = 12.

location.where: Results 3.2, paragraph 2 (post hoc, stage 3, LC value)
location.quote: RR was higher at stage 3 in WC than in LC (26.8 ± 2.7 vs. 23.3 ± 3.7 bpm, p = 0.012, Figure 2)

left_out.what: water-based cycling day (WC): every value of that day (rest HR and VO2 in Table 1, WC column; RR at stage 3, 26.8 ± 2.7 breaths/min, Results 3.2; the WC spirometry and breathing data); the day is immersion to the xiphoid in 31-32 °C water on an underwater bicycle (Methods 2.3)
respiratory rate at rest and at stages 1 and 2 of land cycling, and at rest of the water day (Figure 2 only; the text gives stage 3 of each day alone)

ventilation (VE) and total breathing time (Ttot), rest and stages, both days (Figure 2 only)
Borg rating of perceived exertion, rest and stages, both days (Table 1, RPE block)

oxygen uptake at stages 1 to 3 of land cycling (Table 1, VO2 blocks): used as the bout's intensity input in the protocol, so not also a finding; and %VO2peak at each stage (Table 1), a ratio of the same VO2 to the peak

heart rate at stages 1 to 3 of land cycling (Table 1, HR block; 112 ± 16 bpm at stage 3): HR was read at 2 and 4 min of each stage and averaged (Methods 2.4.1), and the paper says steady VO2 took about 3 min to reach after each change of load (Methods 2.3); only the metabolic and breathing variables are given a steady-state window (last 30 s), HR is not, so the 2-min reading is not a steady-state value
